# EmptyOS Tiers & Packages

> Release manifest v0.8.0 · 4 tiers · 4 platforms · 2 targets.

A **tier** is a named app/plugin/skill bundle in [`release.toml`](../release.toml). `core` and `standard` are the only platform tiers. Every other tier is a packaged distribution/profile for a concrete audience or operating context. `python scripts/package-release.py <tier>` produces a self-contained bundle. Tiers compose via `extends`; the counts below are the *resolved* sets (parent + own). This doc is generated by `scripts/generate_tiers_doc.py` — see [DOC-SYSTEM.md](DOC-SYSTEM.md).

## At a glance

| Tier | Name | Kind | Audience | Scope | Delivery | Extends | Apps | Plugins | Skills | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **core** | EmptyOS Core | platform | Kernel-level EmptyOS install | public | extended-by only (union base for the tiers that extend it) | - | 13 | 2 | 0 | Minimum OS — vault basics, task management, search, generic home |
| **standard** | EmptyOS Standard | platform | Default public/community install | public | targets.public, targets.desktop, products/desktop-windows, products/desktop-macos | core | 73 | 27 | 19 | Full community OS — productivity, AI, creative (end-user value) |
| **demo** | Demo | operational | Public VPS showcase | internal | none - documentation only; the live demo ships via targets.public then demo.hide_apps | core | 30 | 3 | 0 | VPS showcase — core + narrative apps, cloud LLM only |
| **englishos** | EnglishOS | distribution | English learners | public | targets.public (the public snapshot carries every PUBLIC_TIERS tier) | standard | 75 | 28 | 19 | Open English-learning edition — dictionary lookup with local suggestions, and sound-by-sound listening drills. Extends standard. |

**Delivery** is how a tier actually reaches a user — a `[targets.*]` entry, a `products/*/product.toml`, a Dockerfile, or nothing. 1 tier here reads `none`: It exists as a folder invariant for `check-tier-folder.py` and as documentation, and package only on demand via `package-release.py <tier>`. That is a real state, not a defect — but before this column you could only discover it by grepping the repo, which is how a tier stays under-used without anyone noticing.

## Product Map

| Product line | Tier(s) | Audience | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| EmptyOS | `core`, `standard` | Personal and community users | The trunk: the general-purpose OS every branch builds on. |
| EnglishOS | `englishos` | English learners | An open edition (dictionary + listening drills) in the public release; the full learning bundle and hosted learner daemons are held. |

## Platforms

Deployment profiles. Plugins declare compatibility; tiers with a `target_platform` auto-filter incompatible plugins at package time.

| Platform | Capabilities | Description |
|---|---|---|
| **laptop** | gpu, camera, mic, desktop | Local dev machine — GPU, camera, mic, desktop apps |
| **vps-cpu** | — | Cloud VPS, CPU only (Hetzner CX23, DO $6 droplet) |
| **vps-gpu** | gpu | Cloud GPU droplet (DO GPU, RunPod, Lambda) |
| **docker** | — | Container, no hardware assumptions |

## Release targets (distributions)

Where a tier is shipped. `strip_personal` removes machine-specific content; `strip_branding` removes third-party brand names.

| Target | Tier | Repo | Visibility | Strip personal | Strip branding | Deploy |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **public** | englishos | `KevinBean/emptyos` | public | True | True | vps:git-reset+rebuild (demo.binbian.net) |
| **desktop** | standard | `KevinBean/emptyos` | public | True | True | github-releases (zip + latest-emptyos-desktop.json) |

---

Build a tier: `python scripts/package-release.py <tier> --check`. Add a new package by adding a `[tiers.<name>]` block to `release.toml` — the packaging script handles arbitrary tiers. See [RELEASING.md](RELEASING.md) and [DEPLOYMENT.md](DEPLOYMENT.md).
